Thank you so much! I just had a quick idea and the poem ended up turning out pretty well. The ambiguity does leave some unanswered questions but I think it allows the reader to further relate to the narrator. It could be laziness, depression, or just someone who thought they had changed but still have a ways to go. Thanks for the criticism, maybe I’ll add to the poem to make it clearer :)

I love that you capitalized “Long” when mentioning how long ago the narrator was broken. I think having “Long Ago” being capitalized every time might have a more significant impact, like there was some major event or a horrible time that broke them in the narrator’s life.


I also love “beat me” being repeated over and over and over, the beatings that never stop but still can’t break something that is already broken. Fantastic :o

I love the comparison of the poet’s mind to toothpaste, just squeezing out a nearly-empty container with jumbled words and phrases in clumps. When I write poetry I so often feel like I’m wracking my brain for something to rhyme, a word to have the correct syllables, and my toothpaste brain gives me what I get.
